purpose: Inert research and evidence metadata for deterministic contracts; not an executable manifest, rule catalog, dependency audit or finding feed.
relationship_to_existing_corpus: Eight additional advisories; the twelve-advisory frontier and previously executed cases retain their own evidence records.
source_attribution: Version metadata comes from the cited CNA records. EEF CNA data is CC BY 4.0. Contract proposals and patch summaries are Rampart analysis; upstream source code is not vendored.

interpretation.revision_pair: The parent is a candidate pre-fix snapshot, not an executed proof of vulnerability or a complete branch backport map.
interpretation.static_facts: Localization inputs to consider, not claims that current SAST extracts every listed relationship or proves attacker control.
interpretation.refutation_scope: Only the exact declared claim, fixture, controls, case set and budget; no universal absence claim.
interpretation.tool_failures: Host scope denial, harness deadline/cancellation and crashes remain tool failures. A completed validator may record a probe timeout as inconclusive.
interpretation.authority: Subject resolution, executable callbacks, targets, budgets and artifact access must come from host-owned Core.Validation.Binding values. Never restore them from this catalog or a transcript.

entries.title: Resource limits use explicit units
entries.prerequisite: An Ash string constraint accepts caller-supplied text and acts as a storage/resource bound without an independent effective byte or codepoint bound.
entries.patch_observation: The patch adds explicit length-count units and configuration across string types, validations and query functions.
static_facts_to_localize: Package ownership and exact version of Ash string APIs
Length-count options, their configuration provenance, and calls into persistence

proposed_contract.invariant: A value admitted under a declared resource limit must satisfy that limit in its declared unit at the persistence/output boundary.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: Use bounded ASCII, multibyte and combining-mark values around a host-chosen limit. Compare validation with an independent byte/codepoint measurement; separately label intentional grapheme-only UI policies.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap generated input bytes, cases, persisted rows and cleanup time before execution; record both logical length and serialized bytes.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: A completed execution admits a value exceeding the declared resource bound and demonstrates the relevant downstream write or output.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared cases satisfy the resource policy, with accepted in-budget and rejected over-budget controls.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: The storage policy, downstream effect, unit configuration or required execution is unavailable.

required_controls: ASCII limit minus one, equal and plus one
Multibyte codepoints and bounded combining sequences

uncertainty: A grapheme count is not a byte bound. The local SAST diagnostic analogy is a source-review follow-up, not a demonstrated denial of service.

implementation.remaining_scope: Reduced emitted-value model only; actual Ash literal/atomic paths, persistence and runtime configuration are unexecuted.

entries.title: Every incremental parser state has a buffer budget
entries.prerequisite: A Mint HTTP/1 client consumes an untrusted response with an incomplete status line or chunk metadata.
entries.patch_observation: The patch applies the configured response-line size check before retaining additional incomplete status/chunk metadata.
static_facts_to_localize: Mint package ownership and HTTP/1 option provenance
Parser state transitions, concatenation and retained-buffer writes

proposed_contract.invariant: Every incomplete parser state rejects input beyond its declared retained-byte budget, regardless of transport segmentation.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: A host-owned response driver delivers the same bounded byte stream under several chunk partitions and inspects parser acceptance, retained bytes and cleanup.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap input bytes, chunk count, driver processes and scenario duration. Enforce a buffer bound independently of elapsed-time limits.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: A completed scenario retains more bytes than the declared state budget under the stated configuration.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared partitions respect the state budget, including valid and exact-boundary controls.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: Retained state cannot be measured or a harness failure prevents observing the boundary.

required_controls: Limit minus one, equal and plus one

uncertainty: This fix does not establish a bound on numeric parse work; preserve the separate CVE-2026-82729 contract.

implementation.remaining_scope: Reduced line accumulator measures logical retained bytes; actual Mint HTTP grammar, connection lifecycle, transient allocation and worker cleanup are unexecuted.

entries.title: Numeric parsing bounds work before conversion
entries.prerequisite: A Mint HTTP/1 client parses a chunk-size digit sequence supplied by a remote peer.
entries.patch_observation: The parser rejects an additional hexadecimal digit after sixteen digits, bounding the integer accumulator.
static_facts_to_localize: Numeric-fold recursion and incremental parser re-entry

proposed_contract.invariant: Numeric fields are bounded before arbitrary-precision conversion, and fragmented delivery stays within a declared work budget.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: Generate bounded numeric fields around the accepted digit limit and replay bounded partitions. Check rejection independently of parser output; record work counters where available.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap digits, total bytes, partitions, cases and reductions or elapsed time. Timing observations alone do not prove asymptotic complexity.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: A completed execution violates the declared digit or measured-work contract under an independently calibrated oracle.
completed_domain_results.refuted: The declared case set respects the digit/work budgets with valid numeric controls.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: Instrumentation cannot distinguish target work from harness noise, or execution does not complete with usable evidence.

required_controls: Largest allowed digit count and one extra digit

uncertainty: The selected first parent is exactly the CVE-2026-82728 buffer fix. Preserve this ordering so the CPU contract is evaluated independently.

implementation.remaining_scope: Reduced counted hexadecimal folds with prior buffer cap preserved; actual Mint CPU behavior and bignum cost are unmeasured. No asymptotic complexity claim.

entries.title: Malformed input releases workers across segmentation
entries.prerequisite: The OTP inets httpd service accepts chunked request bodies; malformed chunk data reaches the continuation path after headers.
entries.patch_observation: The request continuation changes from a bare catch to structured exception handling that stops the request worker on a chunk decoding error.
static_facts_to_localize: inets ownership and exact component/runtime version
Continuation callbacks, timer cancellation and termination paths

proposed_contract.invariant: Equivalent malformed requests terminate their request workers and release associated resources within a declared cleanup interval under every declared partition.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: In a disposable local httpd fixture, establish baseline workers, deliver bounded malformed requests with controlled segmentation, and inspect worker lifecycle and connection cleanup.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap connections, input bytes, partitions and worker count; use separate execution and cleanup deadlines plus external process termination.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: A completed lifecycle observation shows a request worker surviving beyond the declared cleanup contract with attributable request state.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared partitions release their workers and resources, while a valid request control succeeds.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: Worker attribution or delivery partitioning is unobserved, or cleanup observation is interrupted.

required_controls: Peer disconnect and ordinary request timeout

uncertainty: A harness timeout alone does not prove a worker leak. A pure reduced contract is a separate evidence level from executing the OTP service.

entries.title: Equivalent resource names retain authorization
entries.prerequisite: An inets httpd installation uses mod_auth to protect a directory whose files remain reachable through an alternate path spelling.
entries.patch_observation: The patch collapses repeated path slashes before authorization/file resolution and adjusts directory matching.
static_facts_to_localize: httpd mod_auth configuration and module ownership
Path normalization, alias resolution and authorization call candidates

proposed_contract.invariant: Two requests independently shown to address the same protected resource must retain the same authorization requirement.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: Create a local protected canary file, prove resource identity with an authorized control, and compare unauthenticated requests across host-approved equivalent path spellings.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap local requests and path bytes; use a temporary fixture root, explicit canary identity, connection deadlines and deterministic teardown.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: An unauthenticated variant returns the protected canary while the canonical unauthenticated control is denied.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared equivalent variants preserve the authorization requirement and authorized controls reach the canary.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: Resource equivalence, protected-directory configuration or response identity cannot be established.

required_controls: Non-equivalent path kept outside the equivalence class

uncertainty: Do not assume encoded slashes, case changes or dot segments identify the same resource on every platform. The native filesystem semantics are part of the fixture.

entries.title: Destination policy matches the consuming parser
entries.prerequisite: Caller-controlled text reaches LiveView redirect/2 as a local destination and the browser consumes the LiveView redirect message.
entries.patch_observation: The local URL rejection list gains control-character and tab-related forms that affect browser URL interpretation.
static_facts_to_localize: LiveView redirect/2 ownership and package version
Destination construction and local-policy guard candidates

proposed_contract.invariant: Every accepted local redirect remains within the declared destination policy after the actual consumer resolves it.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: A host-owned LiveView fixture captures the redirect message and a reviewed browser/WHATWG-compatible consumer resolves it against a fixed origin; compare the resolved destination with an independent origin policy.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap destination bytes, cases, browser processes and navigation time; record destination resolution without visiting external hosts.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: An accepted local redirect resolves outside the declared origin policy under the specified consumer.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared cases remain within policy, with valid local and ordinary rejected external controls.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: The actual consumer semantics or redirect route is unavailable, or the fixture substitutes an unverified URL parser.

required_controls: Bounded tab, CR and LF forms

uncertainty: The GitHub affected-version table includes 1.0.19 while also listing it as patched; the EEF structured record uses lessThan 1.0.19. Preserve the discrepancy and prefer exact revisions for future fixtures.
The advisory details distinguish redirect/2 from push_navigate, push_patch and push_redirect. Do not transfer the external-navigation claim to every API sharing a helper.
Elixir URI.parse alone is not a browser-semantics oracle.

entries.title: Effects require the authenticated protocol state
entries.prerequisite: An OTP SSH server accepts a protocol sequence before authentication and exposes connection-layer operations.
entries.patch_observation: The connection handler rejects server-side connection messages while the authenticated flag is false.
static_facts_to_localize: SSH server configuration and package/runtime ownership
Protocol handlers, state guards and effect callback candidates

proposed_contract.invariant: Connection-layer effects cannot occur before authentication, including when messages arrive in an unexpected order.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: Use bounded StreamData event lists and a host-owned disposable SSH fixture with a harmless callback counter. Inspect effects before and after an explicit authentication transition.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Cap event count, encoded bytes, connections and execution time; prohibit arbitrary target command callbacks in the fixture.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: A completed unauthenticated sequence invokes the protected harmless callback.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared unauthenticated sequences produce no protected effect and the authenticated positive control invokes the callback.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: Authentication state, callback attribution or sequence delivery is not observable.

uncertainty: Generate scenarios on StreamData; do not introduce a replacement state-machine or shrinking engine. The full SSH service requires an external fixture, not Core-owned protocol types.

entries.title: Native length arithmetic rejects unrepresentable totals
entries.prerequisite: A TCP socket uses the inet driver with packet mode 4 and processes lengths that reach signed native buffer arithmetic.
entries.patch_observation: Native packet and buffer code checks representable limits before length addition.
static_facts_to_localize: ERTS version provenance and the native boundary associated with socket calls

proposed_contract.invariant: Length headers and accumulated buffer sizes are rejected before native arithmetic overflow or allocation beyond the host budget.
proposed_contract.bounded_experiment: First model bounded integer boundaries with an independent arithmetic oracle. Any later native reproduction requires a disposable process and explicit OS memory/process/time limits; label model evidence separately.
proposed_contract.required_budget: Never allocate payloads near the native integer limit in an in-process Rampart run. Native execution remains blocked on a reviewed externally bounded fixture.

completed_domain_results.confirmed: A completed model case violates the model invariant, or an isolated native case produces an attributable failure; these must be different claim scopes.
completed_domain_results.refuted: All declared boundary cases satisfy the particular model or native contract; neither scope establishes universal runtime safety.
completed_domain_results.inconclusive: Native isolation, version provenance or attribution is unavailable; a model-only result cannot resolve the native claim.

required_controls: First unrepresentable sum in the arithmetic model
Ordinary small valid native packet, if later authorized

uncertainty: The patched C sources are outside the current Elixir/Erlang SAST parser.
The advisory establishes a VM-crash concern; do not label this a demonstrated RCE capability.
